summary: Toshio Nagahiro was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from Kyoto University. He served as professor at Kyoto University (~1950–1969) and president of Kyoto Tachibana University (1978–1986).

Toshio Sako is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikidō Takasaki and Yasunori Ejima, and completed doctoral studies at Columbia University under Alex Wayman.

Toshio Yamazaki was a specialist in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as professor and professor emeritus at the University of Tokyo (~1956–1977) and as professor at Chuo University (~1977–1987).

Toshiya Unebe is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Musashi Tachikawa. He served as an associate professor in the Department of Indian Studies at Nagoya University (attested 2009).

Totsudo Kato was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Seiran Ouchi, Enryo Inoue, and Bankon Shimada. He held teaching posts at Toyo University (~1899), Komazawa University, and Nihon University.

Touraj Daryaee is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and archaeological history. He studied at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1993–1999) and held a post at the University of California, Irvine (~2007).

Towao Sakaehara is a historian and Japanologist who earned his doctorate from Kyoto University. He served as a professor at Osaka City University (1994, 2001–2010) and later as director of the Osaka Museum of History (2014–2020).

Travis L. Smith is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD from Columbia University under John Stratton Hawley. He has taught at Barnard College, the University of Florida, and the University of California, Berkeley.
Trent Walker is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Alexander von Rospatt.

Trevor Leggett worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and philosophy. He studied at King's College London, SOAS, and under Hari Prasad Shastri and Arthur Waley, later heading the BBC Japanese Service (~1946–1970) and lecturing for the Buddhist Society.

Trijang Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Gyuto Monastery and under masters including Pabongkhapa Dechen Nyingpo, later teaching numerous prominent figures, including the 14th Dalai Lama.
Trine Brox is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed her MA under Christian K. Wedemeyer. She holds a post as associate professor at the University of Copenhagen (attested 2026).
Trinle Lhundrub studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Troy Organ was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Iowa. He held academic posts at Parsons College (~1944–1946), the University of Akron (~1946–1954), and Ohio University (1954).

Trulshik Rinpoche was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, and his students included the 14th Dalai Lama and Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche.
Trung Huynh is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of the West under the supervision of Darui Long (attested 2016).

Trungram Gyaltrul Rinpoche is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute and earned a PhD from Harvard University (~1997–2004) under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.

Trungram Gyalwa Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. After studies at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and a PhD from Harvard (-2004), he held visiting posts at the University of Michigan and McGill University (2016).

Tryambak Shankar Shejwalkar was an Indian historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Mumbai (~1913–1917) and served on the faculty at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1939–1955).
Tré Khen Zur Lozang Wangchuk studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Trijang Rinpoche, and the 14th Dalai Lama.
